newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals down, bullion below $380.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals down, bullion below $380.

text.p: Tokyo precious metals futures, except for palladium, settled lower on Thursday, pressured by weak spot prices and the yen's rebound against the dollar, while spot gold fell below a $380.0 support, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from two to 13 yen per gram lower, with most-active benchmark October 12 yen down at 1,368 yen.
Bullion was marked down by fairly large-lot Australian producer selling during Asian hours.
Spot gold was quoted easier at $379.05/35 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $380.15/380.55 in New York on Wednesday.
"Amid bearish sentiment in spot gold, nobody was willing to buy gold. Gold may probe a downside support of $377.0 to $378.0 in the near future," a senior dealer of a foreign bank said.
A lack of inflationary concerns and limited declines in the Dow Industrial Average on Wednesday, were cited as bearish factors for the bullion market, the traders said.
Gold futures ended at the lower side of the day's range as selling by trade houses overwhelmed bargain-hunting by private investors.
Traders said sentiment in spot platinum was also weak, and one trader said it would be a matter of time before spot platinum falls below $380.0 per ounce.
Spot platinum was quoted at $380.25/381.00 at the Tokyo close. Platinum futures ranged from seven to 14 yen per gram lower. Benchmark October was 14 yen lower at 1,380 yen.
Benchmark silver October was 14 yen down at 1,380 yen.
Benchmark palladium October finished up two yen at 426 yen.
